text:
Peverell Semiconductors cut 1,200 staff on Tuesday, about 9% of its workforce, as demand softened across its memory-chip and power-unit lines. Chief executive Mara Vint told employees the reductions would be spread across its Bracken, Tallow, and Northgate sites, with most roles removed from manufacturing and back-office functions. The company said quarterly revenue fell 14% to 2.8 billion crowns, while inventory days rose to 71 from 54 a year earlier.

Peverell also trimmed full-year capital spending to 410 million crowns, down from 560 million. For the sector, the move signals a wider reset: chipmakers are protecting margins by cutting headcount and delaying expansion until industrial orders recover.
